evidence.observation: TeamPCP compromise of LiteLLM (PyPI, ~3.4M daily downloads) March 26, 2026. Same group hit Trivy, KICS, Telnyx.
evidence.notes: Significant scale and breadth of campaign. Diagnostic for whether targeting is AI-strategic or opportunistic.

evidence.observation: TeamPCP target mix is not AI-pure — security tooling + comms + AI lib, suggesting opportunistic high-traffic targeting rather than strategic AI ecosystem targeting.
evidence.notes: Strongly diagnostic for distinguishing strategic vs opportunistic supply chain attack patterns.

evidence.observation: AI recruiting startup Mercor breached through LiteLLM dependency, not own code — example of downstream blast radius.
Vercel breach (April 2026) — CEO publicly attributed attacker velocity to AI augmentation; OpenAI flagged leaked key 9 days before disclosure.
CISA/NSA/Five Eyes joint guidance on agentic AI in OT (April 29, 2026); follow-on to December 2025 advisory.
CISA 'CI Fortify' (May 2026) explicitly links Volt Typhoon-style Chinese pre-positioning to AI-mediated future effects.
Volt Typhoon documented pre-positioning in U.S. critical infrastructure since at least 2019; not eradicated despite multi-year efforts.
evidence.notes: Predates AI but establishes nation-state pre-positioning playbook.

evidence.observation: Vendor claim: 'AI-enabled attacks rose 89% YoY'; 'AI agent compromised 600+ firewalls across 55 countries'.
evidence.notes: High manipulation risk. Statistics without methodology.

evidence.observation: Prompt injection in production agents documented as primary threat to AI infrastructure of past year (CIO analysis).
'ZeroClock' trend — AI-driven vulnerability discovery accelerating; criminals approaching nation-state capability.

Anthropic disclosed (Nov 2025) Chinese state-sponsored actor (GTG-1002) using Claude Code to conduct ~30 autonomous large-scale intrusion operations across tech, finance, chemical, government targets.
evidence.provenance: Direct vendor disclosure with technical detail
evidence.notes: Strongest single piece of evidence for nation-state AI weaponization.

evidence.observation: Hugging Face / model registry trojan disclosures ongoing since 2023; mostly low-skill cryptominers and credential stealers, not sophisticated payloads.
evidence.provenance: Pattern observation across multiple vendor disclosures

evidence.observation: Most published prompt-injection-against-production-agent demos are red-team and academic researchers, not attributable adversary operations.
CISA/NSA agentic AI guidance framed as future risk requiring zero-trust now, not active widespread exploitation.
AI security startup funding volume creates strong commercial incentive to characterize incidents as AI threats.
PLA 2020 Science of Military Strategy codifies 'intelligentization' (智能化) as defining paradigm of future conflict — AI, autonomy, cognitive operations as core to PLA modernization.
evidence.provenance: Academic + CNAS testimony on doctrinal documents
evidence.notes: Strongest authorial-position evidence for nation-state strategic intent.

evidence.observation: PLA doctrine defines AI-driven cognitive warfare as systematic use of AI + big data analytics + psychological operations to manipulate enemy perceptions, integrated with 'Three Warfares' framework.

Anthropic GTG-1002 framing was measured: 'Claude's offensive use exhibited important limitations, including instances in which the model overstated its progress or generated fabricated credentials.' Fully autonomous attacks 'not likely for now'.
evidence.notes: Meta-evidence: vendor disclosure that understates capability is more credible than one that overstates.

evidence.observation: Sonatype tracked 16,279 new malicious packages across npm/PyPI/Maven Central, total past 845,000 — 188% YoY rise in malicious package volume.
evidence.notes: Establishes context: AI-adjacent supply chain attacks are part of broader, accelerating pattern.

evidence.observation: Mini-Shai-Hulud worm credential-harvest scope: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, dev tools, CI/CD pipelines, AI tools, crypto wallets, messaging apps, VPN configs, shell history — AI in basket of ~10 credential categories.

TeamPCP campaign Feb-May 2026: Trivy/KICS/Telnyx → LiteLLM → mass TanStack/Mistral AI SDK/Guardrails AI/SAP CAP/Intercom. Bulk scope targeting pattern (5 malicious versions across 20 packages in @squawk scope).
evidence.notes: Bulk scope targeting is signature of opportunistic mass-compromise.

evidence.observation: Historical pattern: PyTorch torchtriton (Dec 2022 dependency confusion), polyfill.io (June 2024 domain takeover), Lottie Player (npm maintainer compromise) — same TTPs, AI-adjacent packages just newer entries in basket.

WormGPT/FraudGPT emerged mid-2023 — within ~6 months of ChatGPT public release. Pattern: criminal tooling adapts to popular new tech within ~6-12 months, primarily for social engineering / credential theft, not novel attack classes.
SOCRadar purchased access to current WormGPT-branded service, tested it, found experience 'mediocre at best' with threat potential but explicitly not autonomous criminal superintelligence.
evidence.notes: Direct capability assessment of criminal AI tooling. Strong counterevidence to inflated capability narratives.

evidence.observation: February 2026 BreachForums post leaked full wormgpt.ai user database — 19,000 users, emails, payment data, subscription records. Criminal AI ecosystem has poor opsec.
Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit disrupted Storm-2139 — global network using stolen API keys from Azure OpenAI and other legitimate AI services to bypass risk governance.
evidence.notes: Criminal AI access pattern is mostly stolen credentials on legitimate models, not custom AI builds.

evidence.observation: GTG-1002 used Claude Code + open-source pentest tools, NOT custom AI malware. Anthropic: 'minimal reliance on proprietary tools or advanced exploit development.'
GTG-1002 limitation: Claude hallucinations interfered with attack — fabricated credentials, overstated progress. Fully autonomous attacks 'not likely for now' per Anthropic.
Trend Micro 2026 assessment: 'The 2026 outlook is not apocalyptic; it's incremental. We will not see a sudden explosion of AI-driven chaos.'
Picus 2025 Red Report: no notable uptick in AI-driven malware techniques in 2024; 'AI enhances productivity but doesn't yet redefine malware.' Empirical telemetry.
evidence.notes: Strongest empirical counterevidence to 'AI threats exploding' narrative.

evidence.observation: AI-native security market attracted $4.1B VC in 2026, 47% YoY growth; named most-funded cybersecurity segment.
Gartner: AI Cybersecurity segment from $10.82B (2024) to $172B (2029), 73.9% CAGR. Agentic AI security spending projected $201.9B in 2026.
7AI raised $130M Series A at $700M valuation — largest cybersecurity Series A in history. Noma Security $100M for 'AI agent hardening.' WitnessAI $58M.
M&A: Check Point acquired Lakera (AI-native security); Palo Alto acquired Protect AI. Platform vendors buying MCP security before standalone startups reach Series A.
78% of enterprises plan to increase cyber spend in 2026 (industry survey, n=3,887 across 72 countries).
Predicted top AI threats for 2025 (deepfakes, AI voice spoofing) turned out less commonplace than traditional phishing and ransomware despite 53% of pros rating them high/critical.
evidence.notes: Diagnostic predicted-vs-realized gap.

evidence.observation: 2025 prediction 'no extended nation-state outages of major internet/service providers' verified correct; 'catastrophic scenario many feared simply didn't materialize.'
GTG-1002 operators social-engineered Claude with framing 'we're a cybersecurity firm conducting defensive testing' — direct operational tradecraft attested via Anthropic investigation.
evidence.notes: Threat actor utterance evidence that distinguishes deliberate adversarial tradecraft from opportunistic exploitation.

evidence.observation: WormGPT/FraudGPT marketing materials advertise capability ceiling: BEC, phishing, malware generation, vulnerability research — not novel attack classes against AI infrastructure.
TeamPCP attacker payload included taunting domain git-tanstack[.]club signed 'TeamPCP' — opportunistic ego signaling typical of credential-harvesting crews, not state-disciplined operators.
Foresiet headline framing: 'The AI Inversion: 2026's Most Dangerous Cyber Attacks' + claim 'AI-enabled attacks rose 89% YoY' — packaging dramatic, methodology absent.

Same incident framed differently: NeuralTrust calls TeamPCP/LiteLLM 'AI-driven supply chain attacks'; Zscaler/The Register/RapidFort characterize it as conventional supply chain campaign that hit AI-adjacent libraries.
evidence.notes: Taxonomic disagreement on identical incidents is direct evidence of narrative pressure.

evidence.observation: Speculative quantification: 'AI-driven attacks expected to dominate 50% of the threat landscape' — no stated methodology, repeated downstream.

GTG-1002 disclosure (Nov 13-14, 2025) amplified by Cybersecurity Dive, ExtraHop, INE, Help Net Security, Hacker News, Paul Weiss, Lowenstein within ~10 days — mostly faithful to Anthropic's measured framing.
Anthropic disclosure triggered formal House Homeland Security Committee request for Amodei testimony Nov 26, 2025 — substantive institutional amplification.
$4.1B annual AI-security VC funding (E31) requires continued investor belief in AI threats. Specialized AI-security funds (Boldstart $250M) need narrative validation.

Anthropic incentive structure: acknowledging Claude misuse trades brand risk for transparency credibility. The measured framing in disclosures (acknowledging hallucination limits, not overclaiming) is diagnostic of credible reporting.
Nation-state motivation: PLA doctrine on AI cognitive warfare provides theoretical basis for exactly the kind of operation GTG-1002 executed. Motive + means + observed trace alignment.
OpenAI has disrupted 40+ malicious networks since publicly reporting began in early 2024; quarterly cadence on misuse reports established.

OpenAI principal investigator Michael Flossman, on record: 'Across every case that we disrupted... what we saw was incremental efficiency gains, not new capabilities. When these adversaries' interactions crossed into clearly malicious territory, our safeguards worked as intended.'
evidence.notes: Vendor source actively deflating threat narrative against commercial interest.

evidence.observation: OpenAI Oct 2025 report: threat actors building AI into existing workflows, not building new workflows around AI. Multi-model usage (ChatGPT + Claude + DeepSeek) common.
Anthropic Threat Intelligence cadence: March 2025, August 2025, November 2025 (GTG-1002), Feb 2026 risk report — quarterly reporting established.
Anthropic Aug 2025 report (per Ironscales characterization): 9-month Chinese campaign against Vietnamese critical infrastructure across 12 of 14 MITRE ATT&CK tactics — distinct from GTG-1002.
evidence.provenance: Secondary characterization of Anthropic primary report
evidence.notes: Needs verification against Anthropic primary document.

evidence.observation: Anthropic Aug 2025 report: 'MCP-powered stealer log analysis' by criminal actor — explicit MCP weaponization by criminal-tier threat actor.
Splunk analysis of GTG-1002: 'You don't need to prepare for autonomous cyberattacks (yet). That is not where the threat landscape is today.'
PoisonedRAG (USENIX Security 2025): 5 carefully crafted documents among millions in knowledge database achieves 90% attack success rate for targeted RAG manipulation. Existing defenses insufficient.

MCPTox benchmark: 20 prominent LLM agents tested against 45 real-world MCP servers and 353 authentic tools. o1-mini showed 72.8% attack success rate. More capable models often more vulnerable. Claude 3.7 Sonnet highest refusal rate at under 3%.
Endor Labs analysis of 2,614 MCP implementations: 82% use file operations prone to path traversal, 67% use APIs related to code injection, 34% command injection vulnerable.
Vulnerable MCP Project tracks 50+ known MCP vulnerabilities; 13 rated critical. Dozens of MCP-related CVE disclosures in first months of 2026.
CVE-2025-53773 — GitHub Copilot RCE, CVSS 9.6; production AI coding assistant remote code execution. Production-system, not theoretical.

SoK paper on agentic AI attack surface (Dehghantanha 2026): systematizes 20+ peer-reviewed studies 2023-2025 covering prompt injection, RAG poisoning, tool exploits, multi-agent emergent threats — academic field now mature.
Documented production incidents: Slack AI indirect prompt injection and ChatGPT memory poisoning — both real, both researcher-disclosed (not adversary-attributed).

postmark-mcp incident September 2025 — FIRST publicly documented in-the-wild malicious MCP server. Paris-based developer 'phanpak' published 15 benign versions, then v1.0.16 injected single line adding hidden BCC to phan@giftshop[.]club. Detected by Koi Security.
evidence.provenance: Multiple independent primary sources including affected party
evidence.notes: Inflection point: first in-the-wild MCP-specific attack. Closes Gap 3 from prior analysis.

evidence.observation: postmark-mcp impact: ~1,500 weekly downloads; ~300 organizations using actively; estimated 3,000-15,000 emails/day exfiltrated including password resets, MFA codes, invoices, internal correspondence.
evidence.provenance: Vendor analysis with affected party corroboration

evidence.observation: postmark-mcp actor profile: single Paris-based developer using real name (phanpak/Jabal Torres), consumer-grade exfil domain (giftshop[.]club), ~10-day exploitation window, broad target set. Opportunistic criminal pattern, NOT state-strategic.
evidence.notes: Critical disambiguation: H6 confirmation, NOT H1.

evidence.observation: postmark-mcp mechanism is structurally MCP-specific: attack succeeds because MCP tools execute autonomously without human review of side effects. A human auditing emails would catch BCC; an AI agent doesn't see the BCC field as anomalous.

CVE-2025-54136 (MCPoison) — persistent code execution flaw in Cursor IDE via MCP tool poisoning. CVE-2025-54135 (CurXecute) — companion tool poisoning vulnerability. Both exploit gap between tool description audited at install vs served at runtime.
Three-CVE chain in Anthropic's own mcp-server-git (CVE-2025-68143, 68144, 68145) — RCE in MCP infrastructure published by the protocol's primary backer.
OX Security disclosure (May 2026): MCP supply chain vulnerability affecting ~150 million downloads, estimated 200,000 vulnerable instances.

GTG-1002 used MCP tools as part of attack framework — Anthropic explicitly notes 'Claude Code and open standard Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools' as orchestration. State actor used MCP for attack orchestration, did NOT attack MCP infrastructure itself.
evidence.notes: Critical asymmetry with E68: state actor USES MCP as platform; criminal actor ATTACKS MCP infrastructure. Different attack archetypes.
